note: Defects observed in a real delivery, each pinned to a fixture and a detector command. A case here is decided by running one command and comparing codes: no agent, no judge, no credits. That is deliberate — for a mechanically decided case, 'optimising for the test' and 'fixing the defect' are the same action, which is the only place in this loop where reward hacking has no room. Behaviour cases that need a judge stay in behavior-cases.json and carry a weaker evidence level.

cases.source_delivery: migai docs/middleware-pipeline/pipeline-host-r2.sdd.md
cases.statement: A mode-dispatching factory declared its return type with the stage parameter instantiated as never, so the public type admitted no registration at all. Every existing gate passed the document: validate, repo-facts and reading-receipt were clean, and the contract recorded CONVERGED with SYNTHESIS, ADVERSARIAL and ACCEPTANCE_TOPOLOGY all PASS.
cases.root_cause: No step in the authoring pipeline read the `**Signatures:**` fence as types. repo-facts.ts:134-145 extracts import specifiers from it and nothing else; PSEUDOCODE_SYMBOL_UNRESOLVED is a regular-expression candidate that never blocks.

evidence.quote: export function createPipeline<TValue>(mode: IMiddlewarePipelineMode, options: IMiddlewarePipelineHostOptions): IMiddlewarePipelineHost<TValue, never>
evidence.why_it_compiles: Method parameters are bivariant, so the implementation returning a concrete host is still assignable to the declared return type. The defect is reachable only at a call site: `p.use(stage)` compares an argument against a parameter of type never, where no bivariance applies.

observed_baseline.note: 75 documents carry no New/Changed API & Typing section at all, so the probe's reach over this corpus is 8 documents. That is a fact about the corpus, not about the detector, and it bounds any claim made from this baseline.

cases.source_delivery: create-sdd worked example against a fixture workspace
cases.statement: An acceptance method runs `npm` against a package whose workspace declares pnpm. The command would resolve a different tree than the one the design was checked against, and nothing else in the document says which manager is authoritative.
cases.why_this_case_exists: `COMMAND_PACKAGE_MANAGER_MISMATCH` had never fired across 444 observations, and 1016 lines of `managers.ts` plus `package-manager.test.ts` exist to serve it and one sibling code. The audit could not tell a dead rule from a rule whose defect this corpus never contains. This case answers that by running it: the code fires on the mismatch and stays silent on the match, so the rule discriminates and the silence was the corpus, not the rule.

cases.source_delivery: create-sdd worked example against a fixture workspace
cases.statement: An acceptance environment names pnpm 8.1 while the workspace pins pnpm 9.0.0 through `packageManager`. The acceptance would run under a toolchain the repository does not use, so a PASS would be evidence about a different environment than the one shipped.
